title: Fuel Indexation (Road Funding) Special Account Bill 2015
short_title: Fuel Indexation (Road Funding) Special Account Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create a Commonwealth special account to reserve the additional net revenue from fuel duty indexation for investment in road infrastructure.
Credits would reflect additional fuel duty receipts after estimated tax credits, grants and similar payments, with the Treasurer determining an amount annually after each financial year.
The money would fund grants to states and territories under written agreements, alongside companion bills indexing fuel excise and equivalent customs duties on imports.
changes: The Treasurer's credit determinations would be published as legislative instruments without parliamentary disallowance.
The Infrastructure Minister could direct transfers to the existing intergovernmental reform fund for road grants.
Commencement of the account would depend on the companion excise and customs indexation legislation.
summary.affected: State and territory governments and the Treasurer would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Labor supported the fuel excise indexation bills after securing a deal to direct the first two years of revenue ($1.1 billion) into the Roads to Recovery program, arguing this would boost jobs and local economies, particularly in regional and outer suburban areas. The speaker also criticised the government for cutting infrastructure investment and freezing financial assistance grants to councils, while committing Labor to future public transport investment.
